propositions: A reader cannot distinguish a close with signature-append failure from one closed with the gate disabled, because gate state is discarded after close and no durable record of expectation exists on the close event.

The completion_expectation enum (8 values: required, disposition, gate_off, gate_unreadable, force_bypassed, local_source, not_certifiable, not_applicable) must be recorded present-only on the *->closed STATUS event in the same locked write as the close, never in a separate audit event.

The expectation is computed by _completion_precheck as the second half of a returned pair, consuming the tri-state GateState from gates.gate_enabled; gate state resolves first, so --force under disabled/unreadable config records gate_off/gate_unreadable (not force_bypassed).
The idea->closed transition path must set not_applicable explicitly in close_ticket, since idea closes bypass _completion_precheck entirely.

A later reader combines durable completion_expectation with durable attestation to distinguish: required+attestation (signed), required+none (signature lost), disposition+any (disposition-signed or lost), anything else (not expected, with reason specified).
The field is backward-compatible and reducer-known; a legacy close event lacking it reduces to state with the key absent (unknown, never guessed).
